method: Read all four complete candidate bodies, DE/EN current descriptions and immediate prerequisites, general and Physics P criteria, and all four current original images. Independently recalculated every numerical result. Informed reused-thread review, not a new blind D review or observed learner performance. No D045 review files were opened.

goals.numericalEvidence: Drag-only explicit Euler: a_i=−0.5v_i, (x1,v1)=(2,3), (x2,v2)=(3.5,2.25) in SI units. dt=3 yields v1=−2, an unphysical reversal of the specified drag-only motion. Falling model a_i=10−v_i yields v=5,7.5,8.75; terminal speed10 and dt1 comparison10 versus7.5 at the same final time are correct.
goals.scopeAndIndependence: HE E.4 original includes friction, terminal speed, difference-quotient models and spreadsheet calculation. The cases change forces and limiting behavior, not merely numbers; spreadsheet construction and step-size checks make performance independent of the image table. No analytic differential-equation solution is required. The named Euler procedure belongs to these supplied concrete cases, not a claim that all numerical models must use it.
goals.bilingualFinding: DE/EN requirements, signs, initial values, units and outcomes agree.

goals.numericalEvidence: Case1: Qc400, ΔS=400/450−1000/900=−2/9 J/K; Qc≥500, W≤500, eta≤0.5. Case2: Qc=300(0.2+800/600)=460 J; W340 J, eta0.425; reversible Qc=W400 J; extra rejected heat60 J.
goals.scopeAndIndependence: Both cases explicitly bind complete cycles, two constant absolute-temperature reservoirs and no other heat/mass flows. Expectations distinguish medium from reservoirs and ideal work storage. The first rejects an energy-conserving but impossible engine; the second quantifies irreversibility at fixed heat input. Both require the currently described energy/entropy derivation, not a new heat-engine duty or merely copied Carnot substitution.
goals.bilingualFinding: DE/EN premises, rejected-heat signs, bounds, reversibility and Celsius limitation agree.

Both require local/total boundary reasoning; the second rejects an unsupported photograph-based order claim. Supplied formulas and idealizations support the existing competence without importing the refrigerator image numbers or requiring a new statistical-mechanics derivation.

goals.numericalEvidence: Equal10kWh useful heat: A2.5kgCO2e, B1.6–3.2kgCO2e, hence ranking not robust. Extended account: at5years A500/B620kg; at20years A1100/B980kg. B saves16kg annually but has200kg higher manufacturing emissions.
goals.scopeAndIndependence: The first case analyzes an uncertain operational emission factor; the second changes the accounting boundary and duration using complete hypothetical data for that expressly limited account. Both require equal service and conditional data-based conclusions. Simple supplied arithmetic remains accessible across stages; no external product research, full life-cycle methodology, technology recommendation or advanced thermodynamic derivation is required.

limitations: This is a substantive four-profile body counterreview, not a new nationwide source/projection audit or human approval.
The author's two invalid reasoning archetypes were corrected by Root to concept and data; the final bound bodies were checked with those valid archetypes.
No canonical, picture, registry, D-record or historical P-record changes were made by this counterreview. Native materializer PASS4 was reported by Root, not rerun here.
